headline: Stan Wawrinka wins the Australian Open
text: Stan Wawrinka beat Rafael Nadal in the final of the Australian Open, his first Grand Slam title, after beating world number two Novak Djokovic on the way. Switzerland now has two Grand Slam champions.

headline: McDonald's stalls: fewer customers in 2013
text: McDonald's reported on 23 January that worldwide sales at existing restaurants rose only 0.2% in 2013, with higher average checks but fewer customer visits; earnings per share rose 4%. Chief executive Don Thompson calls 2013 'a challenging year'.

headline: Another year of 7.7% earnings growth
text: Altria reported on 30 January that adjusted earnings per share grew 7.7% in 2013 to 2.38 dollars, with higher prices and brand-building lifting income in all three of its main businesses. It forecasts 6 to 9% growth for 2014.

headline: Record deliveries and a plan for a giant battery factory
text: Tesla delivered a record 6,892 Model S in the fourth quarter, had positive free cash flow and expects deliveries to grow by more than 55% in 2014. On 26 February it announced 1.6 billion dollars of convertible bonds to help pay for a huge battery factory, the 'Gigafactory', to make cheaper batteries for a mass-market car.
source: Tesla Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2013 Shareholder Letter, 19 February 2014, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312514058778/d676319dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); Tesla 8-K exhibit of 26 February 2014 (convertible notes), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000119312514069704/d685452dex991.htm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Tesla,_Inc. (bonds for the Gigafactory, read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Tesla Model S at the Geneva motor show

headline: Swiss voters back limits on immigration
text: On 9 February Swiss voters accepted the SVP's initiative 'against mass immigration' by 50.3 percent, a margin of 19,526 votes, and a majority of cantons. It requires quotas on immigration within three years, which contradicts the free movement of people agreed with the EU in the bilateral treaties. Brussels warned that free movement is not negotiable.
imageCaption: SVP politicians, among them Albert Rösti and Adrian Amstutz, celebrate the yes to their initiative 'against mass immigration', 9 February 2014

headline: Ukraine's president flees after a winter of protest
text: Ukrainians have protested on the Maidan, the central square of Kyiv, since November, when President Yanukovych refused to sign an agreement with the European Union and turned to Russia, which offered 15 billion dollars and cheaper gas. From 18 to 20 February police and protesters fought in the streets; over the winter 108 protesters and 13 police officers were killed. Yanukovych fled Kyiv on the evening of 21 February, and the next day parliament voted 328 to 0 to remove him.
imageCaption: Revolution of Dignity, 2014

headline: Disney earnings jump 34%
text: On 5 February Disney reported record quarterly earnings, up 34% to 1.03 dollars a share, with double-digit growth in operating income in every business. Revenue rose 9% to 12.3 billion dollars.
imageCaption: Bob Iger, 2019

headline: Satya Nadella becomes chief executive
text: On 4 February Microsoft named Satya Nadella, head of its cloud and enterprise division and at the company since 1992, as chief executive. Bill Gates leaves the chairmanship to become a technology adviser; John Thompson becomes chairman.
imageCaption: Satya Nadella with Bill Gates and Steve Ballmer, Redmond, 4 February 2014

headline: Sony sells its Vaio PCs and spins off TVs
text: Sony announced the sale of its Vaio PC division to the investment fund Japan Industrial Partners and will turn its television business into a separate company. The TV business has lost about 7.8 billion dollars over a decade.
imageCaption: A Sony Vaio laptop

headline: Russia annexes Crimea
text: After Ukraine's pro-Russian president Viktor Yanukovych fled Kiev in February, soldiers without insignia seized Crimea's parliament and key sites. A referendum under occupation on 16 March was declared a vote to join Russia, and Russia annexed the peninsula on 18 March. The United States and the EU imposed sanctions and travel bans, and Russia was suspended from the G8.
imageCaption: President Putin with Crimean leaders at the signing of the treaty on Crimea's accession, Moscow, 18 March 2014

headline: Fraud at Banamex; Citigroup fails the stress test again
text: Citigroup disclosed a $235 million after-tax loss from a fraud at Banamex, its Mexican bank, discovered in February, and cut its 2013 results. On 26 March the Federal Reserve again rejected its capital plan, this time on concerns about the quality of its risk management.
imageCaption: A former Banco Nacional de Mexico (Banamex) building, Mexico

headline: A seven-for-one split and 130 billion dollars for shareholders
text: On 23 April Apple said it will return more than 130 billion dollars to shareholders by the end of 2015, raise its share buyback to 90 billion dollars and its dividend by about 8%, and split its shares seven for one. Apple has paid a dividend again since 2012, its first since 1995.
imageCaption: Apple's headquarters at One Infinite Loop, Cupertino

headline: The Microsoft sale closes; Nokia is a network company
text: The sale of the phone business to Microsoft was completed in April. Nokia now consists mainly of its network equipment arm, its HERE maps and its patent licensing.
imageCaption: Stephen Elop on stage at Nokia's press event, Mobile World Congress, Barcelona, February 2014

headline: Asset swap with GlaxoSmithKline
text: Novartis announced in April that it will buy GlaxoSmithKline's cancer drug business for $16 billion and sell its vaccines business to GSK for $7.1 billion; the two also plan a joint venture in consumer health products.
imageCaption: The GlaxoSmithKline headquarters on the Great West Road, Brentford

headline: Credit Suisse pleads guilty in the US
text: On 19-20 May Credit Suisse pleaded guilty in the United States to conspiring to help American clients evade taxes, and agreed to pay about $2.6 billion in fines and restitution.
imageCaption: Brady Dougan, chief executive of Credit Suisse, is sworn in before a US Senate committee investigating offshore tax evasion, February 2014

headline: Islamic State seizes Mosul and declares a caliphate
text: Fighters of the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant captured Mosul, Iraq's second city, between 4 and 10 June as Iraqi soldiers fled, and swept towards Baghdad. About half a million people fled Mosul. On 29 June the group declared a caliphate across the parts of Iraq and Syria it controls.
imageCaption: A wrecked Humvee in Mosul after the Islamic State attack, 14 June 2014

headline: Record processor shipments
text: On 15 July Intel reported second-quarter revenue of 13.8 billion dollars and net income of 2.8 billion, up 40%, with record quarterly shipments of microprocessors, and said it will buy back 4 billion dollars of shares in the third quarter.

headline: Cisco's sales shrink and it cuts 8% of jobs
text: Cisco reported fiscal-year revenue of $47.1 billion, down 3%, and announced a restructuring that will eliminate about 8% of its global workforce, some 6,000 jobs, with charges of up to $700 million.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/0001193125-14-308403.txt (8-K with press release, read 2026-10-03); https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/858877/0001193125-14-308733.txt (8-K, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Coca-Cola buys a 16.7% stake in Monster Beverage
text: On 14 August Coca-Cola said it will pay 2.15 billion dollars for 16.7% of Monster Beverage, the energy drink maker, with an option to go to 25%. Coca-Cola hands its own energy drinks to Monster, which in turn passes its non-energy drinks to Coca-Cola, and Coca-Cola's bottlers will distribute Monster.

headline: Alibaba: the biggest stock market launch in history
text: Alibaba, China's giant online marketplace, sold its shares on the New York Stock Exchange on 18 September at 68 dollars each and raised 25 billion dollars, more than any company before it and more than Google, Facebook and Twitter raised together. The company, founded in 1999 in Hangzhou by the former English teacher Jack Ma, is valued at 231 billion dollars.
imageCaption: Jack Ma, 2018

headline: Netflix arrives in Switzerland
text: In September the American streaming service Netflix started in Switzerland, Germany, Austria, France, Belgium and Luxembourg. For a monthly fee it shows films and series over the internet, whenever the viewer wants.
imageCaption: Netflix's headquarters, Los Gatos, California

headline: India reaches Mars at the first attempt
text: On 24 September India's Mars Orbiter Mission, launched in November 2013, entered orbit around Mars. India is the first Asian country to get there, and its space agency succeeded at its very first try. The whole mission cost about 73 million dollars: less, as Prime Minister Modi said, than the Hollywood space film 'Gravity'.
imageCaption: Mars Orbiter Mission, 2014
imageCredit: Kevin Gill from Nashua, NH, United States

headline: eBay to spin off PayPal
text: On September 30 eBay announced it will separate PayPal into an independent listed company, as the activist investor Carl Icahn demanded at the start of the year.
imageCaption: PayPal's headquarters in San Jose, California

headline: By one measure, China's economy is now the world's largest
text: New figures from the International Monetary Fund show that, measured by purchasing power, China's economy will be the world's largest in 2014: $17.6 trillion against $17.4 trillion for the United States, about 16.5% and 16.3% of the world's output. Purchasing power takes into account that things cost less in China: a shirt is cheaper in Shanghai than in San Francisco. Measured in dollars at market exchange rates, the US economy is still more than $6.5 trillion larger.
imageCaption: Lujiazui, 2016

headline: The Fed stops buying bonds, but money stays free
text: On 29 October the Fed ended its bond purchases. Since 2008 it has bought bonds worth about 4.5 trillion dollars with money it created. Its interest rate, however, stays where it has been for six years: at zero. The numbers: the Fed's rate 0.1 percent. Inflation 1.7 percent. Unemployment 5.9 percent.
imageCaption: The Fed's interest rate (blue), inflation (red) and unemployment (grey) in the United States, 1975 to October 2014
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

headline: IBM pays to get rid of its chip factories and drops its 2015 target
text: On 20 October IBM agreed to hand its chip manufacturing business to GlobalFoundries and to pay it 1.5 billion dollars over three years, taking a 4.7 billion dollar charge. It also said it no longer expects to earn at least 20 dollars a share in 2015, a target it had promised for years. Chief executive Ginni Rometty said the results were not what IBM expected.
imageCaption: IBM's Blue Gene/Q supercomputer 'Mira' at Argonne National Laboratory

headline: Rio Tinto rebuffed Glencore
text: Glencore confirmed on 7 October that it had informally proposed a merger to Rio Tinto in July and that Rio was not interested. Under takeover rules Glencore cannot bid for Rio for six months unless circumstances change. In April Glencore agreed to sell Las Bambas to a Chinese consortium for about $5.85bn, as China required.

headline: Daimler sells its Tesla stake
text: Daimler sold its remaining shares in the electric car maker Tesla for a reported 780 million dollars. It took almost 10% of Tesla in May 2009, when Tesla was a small private company, and sold part of the stake to its shareholder Aabar later that year. Tesla supplied batteries and motors for electric versions of the Smart and the Mercedes B-Class.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. (Daimler stake, read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 2009 ('Daimler takes a stake in Tesla', 19 May 2009; Aabar, 13 July 2009), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/2009.xhtml?oid=4913607 (read 2026-10-03); The Detroit News, 'Daimler sells 4% Tesla stake', 22 October 2014 (headline via Google News) (read 2026-10-03)

headline: OPEC refuses to cut
text: On 27 November in Vienna, Saudi oil minister Ali al-Naimi blocked calls from poorer OPEC members to cut output, saying the market should find its own level. US crude fell about 10% by 28 November to $65.94, down from $107 in June. US crude output is about 9.3 million barrels a day, up by two thirds in four years. ExxonMobil, which earned more than 32 billion dollars in 2013, fell 6%: every dollar off the oil price cuts its profit.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OPEC (read 2026-10-03); https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=RWTC&f=D (read 2026-10-03); https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=MCRFPUS2&f=M (read 2026-10-03); https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DCOILWTICO (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010s_oil_glut (read 2026-10-03); ExxonMobil press release of 2 February 2015 (2013 and 2014 earnings), https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/34088/000003408815000004/f8k4q991.htm (read 2026-10-03)

imageCredit: Photo by SAMUEL KUBANI/AFP via Getty Images

headline: Federer and Wawrinka win the Davis Cup
text: Switzerland won tennis's Davis Cup for the first time, beating France in the final in Lille from 21 to 23 November. Roger Federer and Stan Wawrinka led the team.

headline: Kaeser starts Vision 2020
text: On 6 November Siemens reported fourth-quarter net income up 40% at 1.5 billion euros and said it has begun carrying out 'Vision 2020', its plan to concentrate on electrification, automation and digitalization and to cut costs by a billion euros. Earlier this year it agreed to buy Rolls-Royce's gas turbine business for 1 billion pounds and, with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, bid against General Electric for Alstom's energy business.

headline: 2014 in review: the S&P 500 passes 2,000
text: The S&P 500 rose 11% in 2014 to 2,058.90, after first closing above 2,000 on 26 August; the Dow gained 7.5%. The Federal Reserve ended its bond-buying programme in October.

headline: Switzerland introduces negative interest rates
text: On 18 December the Swiss National Bank announced that from 22 January banks will pay 0.25 percent a year on large deposits held with it: a negative interest rate, meant to stop the franc from rising further. The European Central Bank began charging banks 0.1 percent on their deposits in June. In America the Fed's rate has stayed near zero since December 2008, and the 10-year Treasury yield averaged 2.2 percent in December, with inflation at 1.3 percent (November). The numbers: the Fed's rate 0.1 percent. Inflation 1.2 percent. Unemployment 5.8 percent.
imageCaption: The Fed's interest rate (blue), inflation (red) and unemployment (grey) in the United States, 1975 to December 2014
imageCredit: Chart: Month by Month. Data: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)

headline: Harald Krüger named as Reithofer's successor
text: BMW said on 9 December that board member Harald Krüger will become chief executive in May 2015, succeeding Norbert Reithofer, who is to move to the chairmanship of the supervisory board.
source: bmwblog, 'Harald Krüger to become BMW's CEO in May 2015', 9 December 2014, https://www.bmwblog.com/2014/12/09/harald-kruger-become-bmws-ceo-may-2015/ (via Google News, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norbert_Reithofer (read 2026-10-03)
